intro: These crops come from German-language daily newspapers printed in Iowa, held by the Library of Congress. They are the human reference for the German comparison (#968): type each one from the print alone. Nothing from any machine is shown or filled in. Zoom in by clicking the image.
name: German: type the crops
rules: Type what is printed, one line of your text for each printed line, in reading order. Keep the printed spelling, capital letters, punctuation and hyphens, and keep ſ (long s) where it is printed; the buttons insert ſ, umlauts and ß. Don't join a word split across lines at a hyphen. If the crop cuts a line at its edge, type only the letters wholly inside it. Type [?] for one letter you can't read, or [?x] for a letter you read as x with doubt. Never skip printed text. Your reading settles the crop.
title: German: type the crops
